entries.name: Section drawings
entries.definition: Preparing or reading drawings that show a building or object as if cut through along a plane, to reveal its internal construction.

entries.name: Secure coding
entries.definition: Writing software in ways that avoid common security flaws, such as injection, unsafe input handling and memory errors.

entries.name: Secure Shell
entries.definition: A network protocol for encrypted remote login and command execution between computers.

entries.name: Secured transactions
entries.definition: The area of commercial law that governs loans and credit backed by collateral in personal property, such as Article 9 of the US Uniform Commercial Code.

entries.name: Security information and event management
entries.definition: Software that gathers and correlates security logs and events from across an organisation so that threats can be detected, investigated and reported.

entries.name: Security management
entries.definition: Planning and overseeing the measures, people and procedures that protect an organisation's people, property and information.

entries.name: Security Onion
entries.definition: A free Linux distribution for network security monitoring, intrusion detection, log management and threat hunting.

entries.name: Security operations
entries.definition: Running the monitoring, detection and response work that keeps an organisation's systems and data secure.

entries.name: Seeder
entries.definition: A farm machine that sows seeds into the soil at a set depth and spacing.

entries.name: Seesaw (software)
entries.definition: A classroom app where students build digital portfolios of their work and teachers share it with families.

entries.name: Segment (software)
entries.definition: A customer data platform, owned by Twilio, that collects event data from websites and apps and sends it to other tools.

entries.name: Selenium
entries.definition: An open-source suite for automating web browsers, mainly used to write automated tests for web applications.

entries.name: Seliwanoff's test
entries.definition: A chemical test using resorcinol and hydrochloric acid that tells ketose sugars, such as fructose, from aldose sugars.

entries.name: Sequel Pro
entries.definition: A free Mac application for managing MySQL and MariaDB databases through a graphical interface.

entries.name: Sequelize
entries.definition: A JavaScript object-relational mapper for Node.js that works with databases such as PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite and SQL Server.

entries.name: Serial ATA
entries.definition: A computer bus interface standard for connecting storage drives such as hard disks and solid-state drives to a motherboard.

entries.name: Serial Line Internet Protocol
entries.definition: A simple protocol that carries IP packets over serial lines such as dial-up modem links, described in RFC 1055.

entries.name: Service desk
entries.definition: Giving users first-line support for IT problems and requests, and logging, resolving or escalating each case.

entries.name: Service level requirement
entries.definition: Defining and recording what a customer needs from a service, such as availability and response time, as the basis for a service level agreement.

entries.name: Service orientation
entries.definition: Looking out for chances to be useful to other people and acting on them.

entries.name: ServiceNow
entries.definition: A cloud platform for IT service management and for automating business workflows.

entries.name: ServiceNow Discovery
entries.definition: A ServiceNow product that scans a network to find devices and applications and records them in the configuration management database.

entries.name: Sex therapy
entries.definition: Counselling or psychotherapy that helps individuals and couples with sexual difficulties and concerns.

entries.name: SHA-256
entries.definition: A cryptographic hash function from the SHA-2 family, specified in NIST FIPS 180-4, that produces a 256-bit digest.

entries.name: SHA-512
entries.definition: A cryptographic hash function from the SHA-2 family, specified in NIST FIPS 180-4, that produces a 512-bit digest.

entries.name: Shaolin kung fu
entries.definition: A family of Chinese martial arts associated with the Shaolin Temple; Sil Lum is the Cantonese rendering of Shaolin.

entries.name: Sharable Content Object Reference Model
entries.definition: A set of technical standards for packaging e-learning content and tracking learners so that courses work across learning management systems.

entries.name: Shared Vision Planning
entries.definition: A collaborative water-resources planning approach that combines traditional planning, stakeholder participation and shared computer models.

entries.name: ShareFile
entries.definition: A cloud service for storing, sharing and collaborating on business files securely, originally from Citrix.

entries.name: Sharp Zaurus
entries.definition: A line of handheld personal digital assistants made by Sharp, many of which run Linux.

entries.name: Shepard's Citations
entries.definition: A LexisNexis legal research service that lists later cases and authorities citing a given case, showing whether it is still good law.

entries.name: Ship handling
entries.definition: Controlling a ship's movement, especially manoeuvring it in confined water and when berthing.

entries.name: Shipping and receiving
entries.definition: Preparing and dispatching outgoing goods and checking, recording and storing incoming goods.

entries.name: Shipping management
entries.definition: Planning and overseeing how goods are packed, dispatched and delivered to customers.

entries.name: Shoulder surgery
entries.definition: Performing or assisting with operations on the shoulder joint, such as rotator cuff repair and joint replacement.

entries.name: Shower installation
entries.definition: Fitting a shower, including its enclosure, valves and drainage, in a bathroom.

entries.name: Shrink wrapping
entries.definition: Packaging items in plastic film that is shrunk tight around them with heat.

entries.name: Shuttle car operation
entries.definition: Driving a shuttle car, the low electric haulage vehicle that carries cut coal or ore from the mining machine to the conveyor in an underground mine.

entries.name: Signalling Connection Control Part
entries.definition: A layer of the SS7 telephone signalling protocol stack that adds addressing and connection-oriented and connectionless services on top of the message transfer part.

entries.name: Signalling System No. 7
entries.definition: A set of ITU-T telephone signalling protocols used to set up and route calls and provide services across public telephone networks.
